  "title": "Beyond Step-Local Verification: Tracing Perception Error Cascades in Multimodal Process Reward Models",
  "core_problem": "Multimodal process reward models verify each reasoning step independently, missing cascade errors: steps where local reasoning is valid but produces wrong results because upstream visual information was misperceived. When a VLM misreads '45 degrees' as '90 degrees' in step 2, steps 3-7 may apply flawless trigonometry to the wrong angle -- appearing locally correct but systematically producing wrong answers. Cascade errors are invisible to binary correct/incorrect labels, to simple perception/reasoning classification (the cascade step's own reasoning IS correct), and even to Perceval's hallucination detection (no hallucination occurs at the cascade step itself). Across 4+ independent studies, 67-87% of VLM errors originate from visual perception, and each perception error can corrupt multiple downstream steps. Yet no existing verification method detects cascade errors: EVPV explicitly flags step-local cascade tracking as future work; MMErroR explicitly excludes cascading errors from evaluation; PARC models accumulation errors but only in text-only settings. Cascade-aware verification requires a fundamentally new capability: dependency-aware step evaluation that traces visual information flow through reasoning chains.",
  "opportunity": "Three converging developments make cascade-aware multimodal PRMs both timely and feasible. (1) The cascade detection gap is now explicitly acknowledged. EVPV/Grounding the Score (March 2026) uses global reliability signals for visual premise verification but states that 'step-local reliability is an important next step' -- precisely our contribution. MMErroR (Jan 2026) explicitly excludes cascading errors from their benchmark, acknowledging the gap without filling it. Hallucination propagation research (arXiv 2603.27201) empirically shows that cascade errors produce 'locally plausible, internally coherent' steps that mask underlying errors, motivating detection. (2) Text-only cascade detection proves the concept. PARC (Feb 2025) models 'accumulation errors' via premise-augmented DAGs in text-only reasoning, distinguishing root-cause from propagated errors. Conditional Reward Modeling (CRM, 2025) captures causal relationships among reasoning steps. ReasonDiag (March 2026) finds ~44.5% of verification false positives stem from error propagation. These demonstrate that dependency-aware verification is valuable -- extending it to the multimodal perception-reasoning boundary is the natural next step. (3) Dimensional and typed PRM approaches have matured but plateaued at step-independent evaluation. GM-PRM evaluates {visual alignment, reasoning logic} independently per step but cannot trace cross-step dependencies. PathFinder-PRM shows typed labels help in text-only (+2.2 PRMBench) but their ablation reveals that hierarchical structure matters more than category labels alone (-2.8 vs -0.4 on PRMBench). Perceval detects hallucinated spans but treats each step independently. The missing capability across all approaches is dependency-aware verification -- and the multimodal setting, where perception errors cascade from visual processing into reasoning chains, creates the strongest need for it.",
  "landscape": "The landscape segments into five clusters, none occupying CascadePRM's position at the intersection of multimodal perception-awareness and dependency-aware verification.

**Cluster A -- Step-Independent Multimodal PRMs.** Training VL-PRMs (arXiv 2509.23250) provides VL-PRM300K (1.32M steps) with binary labels despite noting 86% perception errors. VisualPRM (arXiv 2503.10291) provides VisualProcessBench (26,950 human labels), binary only. DreamPRM-1.5, TIM-PRM, VRPRM, MM-PRM, URSA all produce binary step scores. All evaluate each step independently without modeling cross-step information flow.

**Cluster B -- Perception-Aware Step-Independent Verification.** Perceval (arXiv 2604.24583, April 2026) detects hallucinated spans via token-level binary classification -- closest existing work, but treats each step independently and cannot distinguish cascade errors from direct errors. GM-PRM (arXiv 2508.04088) evaluates {step intent, visual alignment, reasoning logic} as structured CoT for generative scoring, but evaluations are step-independent with no cross-step dependency modeling; dimensions serve as training scaffolding producing a single Final Judgment score, not structured error labels; and no ablation demonstrates the value of separate dimensions. EVPV/Grounding the Score (arXiv 2603.16253) computes visual reliability via checklist verification, but uses candidate-level (global) rather than step-local reliability, and explicitly identifies step-local cascade tracking as future work.

**Cluster C -- Perception-Aware RL Optimization (Downstream).** PAPO (ICLR 2026, arXiv 2507.06448) uses implicit perception loss via masked-image KL divergence in GRPO -- no PRM involvement. VPPO (ICLR 2026, arXiv 2510.09285) reweights by visual dependency tokens. AT-RL (arXiv 2602.11455), PRCO (arXiv 2603.28618), Perception-R1 (ICLR 2026), PDCR (May 2026), and 'Bad Seeing or Bad Thinking' (ICML 2026 Spotlight) all operate at RL reward/policy level. These consume PRM outputs as scalar rewards; cascade-aware PRM outputs would directly improve the quality of signals these methods consume.

**Cluster D -- Text-Only Dependency-Aware Verification.** PARC (arXiv 2502.02362) introduces 'accumulation errors' via premise-augmented DAGs, distinguishing root-cause from propagated errors -- the closest text-only analog to cascade detection, but no multimodal component. CRM (arXiv 2509.26578) captures causal relationships among text reasoning steps via conditional probability chains. ReasonDiag (arXiv 2603.21286) visualizes error propagation patterns in text-only CoT, finding ~44.5% of verification false positives from error propagation. RewardFlow (arXiv 2603.18859) uses topology-aware propagation in state graphs. All are text-only and do not address the perception-reasoning boundary.

**Cluster E -- Error Taxonomies Without Cascade Detection.** PathFinder-PRM (arXiv 2505.19706) uses {math, consistency} types in text-only PRMs with modest gains (+2.2 PRMBench, but ablation shows category separation contributes only -0.4 vs -2.8 for hierarchical structure). ErrorRadar (ICLR 2025 Workshop) provides {visual perception, calculation, reasoning, knowledge, misinterpretation} for benchmarking MLLM error detection -- never for PRM training. MMErroR (arXiv 2601.03331) defines {visual perception, knowledge, comprehension, reasoning} but explicitly states: 'each sample contains a single, coherent reasoning error... real-world reasoning failures often involve cascading or multiple simultaneous errors.' ThinkWithImages-PRMBench (arXiv 2602.08346) defines 7 error types across 4 categories -- none is a cascade error. All taxonomies evaluate errors at the individual step level without modeling cross-step propagation.

**CascadePRM's unique position**: We bridge Cluster B (multimodal perception-aware verification) with Cluster D (dependency-aware verification) to detect cascade errors -- the gap explicitly acknowledged by EVPV, excluded by MMErroR, and unaddressed by any existing multimodal PRM.",
  "inspired_by": "Three conceptual bridges define CascadePRM's contribution. (1) PARC's accumulation error framework proves that distinguishing root-cause from propagated errors improves text-only verification, but the perception-reasoning boundary in multimodal settings creates a far more impactful instance of this problem: upstream perception failures cascade through downstream reasoning in ways that are mechanistically distinct from text-only logical propagation, because the root cause is cross-modal (visual processing failure) while the cascade is within-modal (text reasoning). (2) EVPV's explicit limitation creates our opportunity: their global reliability signal attenuates all steps uniformly when visual reliability is low, but cascade errors require step-local analysis -- a step that doesn't reference the image at all can still be a cascade error if it uses a value derived from an earlier misperception. The EVPV authors themselves identify step-local reliability as the 'important next step.' (3) PathFinder-PRM's ablation reveals that hierarchical structure (error detection guiding reward prediction) matters more than error type labels alone (-2.8 vs -0.4 on PRMBench). This insight shapes our approach: rather than simply classifying error types, we build a dependency-aware hierarchy where cascade detection (which requires reasoning about cross-step information flow) provides richer structural information than flat type classification. The counterfactual formalization -- 'would this step be correct if the upstream perception were corrected?' -- provides an objective, testable definition of cascade errors that avoids the subjectivity concerns of purely categorical error typing.",
  "approach": "We propose CascadePRM, a framework for detecting and leveraging perception error cascades in multimodal reasoning verification, comprising four interlocking components: (1) a counterfactual cascade detection algorithm, (2) a cascade-annotated benchmark and dataset, (3) cascade-aware PRM training, and (4) downstream integration demonstrating infrastructure value.

**Component 1: Counterfactual Cascade Detection Algorithm (Primary Novelty, Weeks 1-7).**

We formalize cascade errors and build an automated detection pipeline in four stages:

(Stage 1) Visual Claim Extraction: For each step in a solution, extract all claims that reference information derived from the image (e.g., 'angle ABC = 45 deg', 'the bar for 2020 shows 3.2M'). Uses a VLM (Qwen2.5-VL-72B) with targeted prompts to identify visual claims vs. pure reasoning statements.

(Stage 2) Information Flow Graph Construction: Build a directed acyclic graph (DAG) where nodes are reasoning steps and edges connect step j to step k if step k uses a quantity, relationship, or fact derived from visual claims in step j (directly or transitively). This extends PARC's premise-augmented DAG framework from text-only logical dependencies to cross-modal visual-to-reasoning dependencies.

(Stage 3) Perception Error Identification: For each step containing visual claims, verify claims against the image using ensemble VLM voting (Qwen2.5-VL-72B, InternVL2.5-78B, Gemini-2.5-Flash). Steps with incorrect visual claims verified by majority vote are labeled as root-cause perception errors. Dedicated perception verification extracts the specific claim and independently checks it with a focused prompt.

(Stage 4) Counterfactual Cascade Verification: For each downstream step k depending (via the DAG) on a root-cause perception error at step j: (a) extract the misperceived value from step j and determine the correct value; (b) construct a counterfactual prompt: 'Given that [quantity] is actually [correct_value] rather than [misperceived_value], is the reasoning in step k valid?'; (c) if the reasoning IS locally valid (confirmed by 2/3 VLMs), label step k as a CASCADE error; (d) if the reasoning is NOT locally valid, label as a direct error (reasoning, calculation, etc.). This counterfactual test provides an objective, testable definition unprecedented in the multimodal PRM literature.

**Component 2: Cascade-Annotated Benchmark and Dataset (Weeks 2-8).**

(Phase A) Gold-Standard Benchmark -- VisualProcessBench-Cascade: Extend VisualProcessBench's 2,866 samples (~8,000 incorrect steps) with cascade annotations. For each incorrect step, annotators (6 graduate-level, STEM backgrounds) assign: (i) a 3-tier error type {perception, reasoning, cascade} as the core taxonomy; (ii) an optional fine-grained subtype for non-cascade errors {perception subtypes: spatial/numerical/object/attribute; reasoning subtypes: symbolic_formulation/calculation/logical_deduction}; (iii) for cascade errors: the root-cause step ID and the misperceived value. Target inter-annotator agreement: Cohen's kappa > 0.65 for 3-tier classification (substantially above chance for 3-way), with agreement reported at all granularity levels: binary, 2-way {root-cause vs. cascade}, 3-tier, and full fine-grained. The cascade category is operationalized via the counterfactual question ('would this step be correct with corrected perception?'), which is more objective than purely categorical error typing.

(Phase B) Large-Scale Dataset -- VL-PRM-Cascade: Apply the automated cascade detection pipeline (Component 1) to VL-PRM300K (1.32M steps). Confidence-calibrated labeling: HIGH confidence (3/3 VLM agreement, ~70-75%) used directly; MEDIUM (2/3, ~15-20%) used with reduced weight; LOW (~10-15%) routed to human review. Validate against gold benchmark, targeting >80% cascade detection F1.

Pre-committed granularity fallback: If 3-tier kappa falls below 0.60, we report the {root-cause error vs. cascade error} binary taxonomy, which should achieve kappa > 0.70 as a binary classification with an objective counterfactual criterion. This turns a potential weakness into a controlled granularity ablation.

**Component 3: Cascade-Aware PRM Training (Weeks 7-12).**

Train multimodal PRMs (InternVL2.5-8B backbone) with five training regimes forming a granularity ladder:

(A) Binary baseline: standard correct/incorrect on VL-PRM300K.
(B) 2-way typed: {perception error, reasoning error} -- the simplest typed approach, similar in spirit to GM-PRM's dimensional separation but as explicit training labels.
(C) 3-way cascade-aware (PRIMARY MODEL): {perception, reasoning, cascade} with a two-stage prediction architecture inspired by PathFinder-PRM's hierarchical insight: first predict error type (perception/reasoning/cascade), then predict correctness conditioned on error type. For cascade errors, the model additionally predicts the root-cause step, providing interpretable error provenance.
(D) 3-way with cascade-weighted loss: same taxonomy as (C) but with cascade-specific loss weighting. Cascade errors receive higher weight because they represent the largest information gain over binary labels (a cascade step is wrong but for external reasons, requiring different correction strategies). Loss: L = sum_i w(type_i) * CE(y_i, y_hat_i) where w(cascade) > w(perception) > w(reasoning).
(E) Full fine-grained (ablation): complete sub-category decomposition for maximal information, reported for completeness.

Compare against: binary VL-PRM-7B, Perceval (binary hallucination PRM), GM-PRM (dimensional CoT), and EVPV (global reliability gating).

**Component 4: Downstream Integration -- EVPV Enhancement (Weeks 10-13).**

Demonstrate that cascade-aware PRM labels improve downstream verification by enhancing EVPV's framework:

(Integration A) Replace EVPV's global reliability signal with CascadePRM's step-local cascade scores. Instead of attenuating all steps uniformly when visual reliability is low, attenuate only steps identified as cascade-dependent (via the information flow DAG). Steps with no visual dependency path are scored at full weight regardless of global reliability.

(Integration B) Cascade-aware advantage weighting for RL: following DRM's multi-dimensional GRPO framework (arXiv 2510.11457), provide separate advantage signals for perception-error steps (which need better visual grounding) and cascade steps (which need upstream correction, not local improvement). This validates that typed PRM signals can improve RL training -- a mechanism proven feasible by Fine-Grained RLHF (NeurIPS 2023) and POW3R (arXiv 2605.20164) but never demonstrated with multimodal error types.

**Phase 5: Evaluation and Ablations (Weeks 10-15).**

Evaluate on: (a) VisualProcessBench-Cascade: step-level F1 for binary correctness, 3-way error type classification, and cascade detection accuracy (precision/recall/F1 specifically for identifying cascade steps); (b) downstream Best-of-N reranking on MathVista, MathVision, WeMath, ChartQA, PuzzleVQA with N=8,16,64; (c) EVPV integration: step-local vs. global reliability on the same benchmarks; (d) cascade-specific analysis: performance stratified by cascade depth (how many steps from the root perception error), visual modality (geometry/charts/tables), and cascade frequency.

Key ablations forming the granularity ladder: (i) {binary} -> {perception vs. reasoning} -> {perception, reasoning, cascade} -> {full fine-grained} to isolate cascade detection's marginal contribution; (ii) with/without counterfactual verification in cascade detection (does the counterfactual step improve over simple dependency-based cascade labeling?); (iii) cascade-weighted vs. uniform loss; (iv) head-to-head vs. GM-PRM's dimensional CoT approach on cascade-heavy problems; (v) annotation quality: high-confidence-only vs. all labels vs. human-verified.

**Expected Results and Contingency.** Primary hypothesis: the 3-way cascade-aware model (C) will outperform binary PRMs by +3-5 on VisualProcessBench step-level F1 and +2-3 on Best-of-N, with disproportionately large gains on geometry and diagram problems where cascade errors are most frequent. The granularity ladder will show that the {perception, reasoning} -> {perception, reasoning, cascade} step provides the largest marginal improvement, validating cascade detection as the primary value driver. EVPV integration will show +1-2 on benchmarks where EVPV already works. Conservative scenario: if overall gains are modest, the cascade error characterization (frequency, depth distribution, modality stratification) and released artifacts (VisualProcessBench-Cascade, VL-PRM-Cascade, cascade detection pipeline) are publishable contributions as the first empirical study of cascade error propagation in multimodal reasoning verification.",

We demonstrate downstream value via EVPV integration, replacing global reliability with step-local cascade-aware scores, and via cascade-aware RL advantage weighting following DRM's multi-dimensional GRPO framework. No existing PRM can distinguish cascade errors from direct errors. The counterfactual test ('would this step be correct if the upstream perception were corrected?') is unprecedented in multimodal PRM literature. Our Integration A replaces global reliability with step-local cascade-aware scores -- steps without visual dependency paths in the DAG are scored at full weight regardless of global reliability, while cascade-dependent steps are attenuated. The information flow DAG explicitly traces the visual-to-symbolic-to-textual pathway. CascadePRM's counterfactual analysis asks exactly the cross-modal integration question: 'if the visual understanding were correct, would the symbolic and textual reasoning succeed?'   "core_problem": "Multimodal process reward models verify each reasoning step independently, missing cascade errors: steps where local reasoning is valid but produces wrong results because upstream visual information was misperceived. Cascade errors are invisible to binary correct/incorrect labels, to simple perception/reasoning classification (the cascade step's own reasoning IS correct), and even to Perceval's hallucination detection (no hallucination occurs at the cascade step itself). These demonstrate that dependency-aware verification is valuable -- extending it to the multimodal perception-reasoning boundary is the natural next step. The missing capability across all approaches is dependency-aware verification -- and the multimodal setting, where perception errors cascade from visual processing into reasoning chains, creates the strongest need for it.",

**Cluster A -- Step-Independent Multimodal PRMs.** Training VL-PRMs (arXiv 2509.23250) provides VL-PRM300K (1.32M steps) with binary labels despite noting 86% perception errors. VisualPRM (arXiv 2503.10291) provides VisualProcessBench (26,950 human labels), binary only. DreamPRM-1.5, TIM-PRM, VRPRM, MM-PRM, URSA all produce binary step scores. All evaluate each step independently without modeling cross-step information flow.

**Cluster B -- Perception-Aware Step-Independent Verification.** Perceval (arXiv 2604.24583, April 2026) detects hallucinated spans via token-level binary classification -- closest existing work, but treats each step independently and cannot distinguish cascade errors from direct errors. GM-PRM (arXiv 2508.04088) evaluates {step intent, visual alignment, reasoning logic} as structured CoT for generative scoring, but evaluations are step-independent with no cross-step dependency modeling; dimensions serve as training scaffolding producing a single Final Judgment score, not structured error labels; and no ablation demonstrates the value of separate dimensions. EVPV/Grounding the Score (arXiv 2603.16253) computes visual reliability via checklist verification, but uses candidate-level (global) rather than step-local reliability, and explicitly identifies step-local cascade tracking as future work.

**Cluster C -- Perception-Aware RL Optimization (Downstream).** PAPO (ICLR 2026, arXiv 2507.06448) uses implicit perception loss via masked-image KL divergence in GRPO -- no PRM involvement. VPPO (ICLR 2026, arXiv 2510.09285) reweights by visual dependency tokens. AT-RL (arXiv 2602.11455), PRCO (arXiv 2603.28618), Perception-R1 (ICLR 2026), PDCR (May 2026), and 'Bad Seeing or Bad Thinking' (ICML 2026 Spotlight) all operate at RL reward/policy level. These consume PRM outputs as scalar rewards; cascade-aware PRM outputs would directly improve the quality of signals these methods consume.

CRM (arXiv 2509.26578) captures causal relationships among text reasoning steps via conditional probability chains. ReasonDiag (arXiv 2603.21286) visualizes error propagation patterns in text-only CoT, finding ~44.5% of verification false positives from error propagation. RewardFlow (arXiv 2603.18859) uses topology-aware propagation in state graphs. All are text-only and do not address the perception-reasoning boundary.

ThinkWithImages-PRMBench (arXiv 2602.08346) defines 7 error types across 4 categories -- none is a cascade error. All taxonomies evaluate errors at the individual step level without modeling cross-step propagation.

  "approach": "We propose CascadePRM, a framework for detecting and leveraging perception error cascades in multimodal reasoning verification, comprising four interlocking components: (1) a counterfactual cascade detection algorithm, (2) a cascade-annotated benchmark and dataset, (3) cascade-aware PRM training, and (4) downstream integration demonstrating infrastructure value.

**Component 1: Counterfactual Cascade Detection Algorithm (Primary Novelty, Weeks 1-7).**

We formalize cascade errors and build an automated detection pipeline in four stages:

(Stage 1) Visual Claim Extraction: For each step in a solution, extract all claims that reference information derived from the image (e.g., 'angle ABC = 45 deg', 'the bar for 2020 shows 3.2M'). Uses a VLM (Qwen2.5-VL-72B) with targeted prompts to identify visual claims vs. pure reasoning statements.

(Stage 2) Information Flow Graph Construction: Build a directed acyclic graph (DAG) where nodes are reasoning steps and edges connect step j to step k if step k uses a quantity, relationship, or fact derived from visual claims in step j (directly or transitively). This extends PARC's premise-augmented DAG framework from text-only logical dependencies to cross-modal visual-to-reasoning dependencies.

(Stage 3) Perception Error Identification: For each step containing visual claims, verify claims against the image using ensemble VLM voting (Qwen2.5-VL-72B, InternVL2.5-78B, Gemini-2.5-Flash). Steps with incorrect visual claims verified by majority vote are labeled as root-cause perception errors. Dedicated perception verification extracts the specific claim and independently checks it with a focused prompt.

(Stage 4) Counterfactual Cascade Verification: For each downstream step k depending (via the DAG) on a root-cause perception error at step j: (a) extract the misperceived value from step j and determine the correct value; (b) construct a counterfactual prompt: 'Given that [quantity] is actually [correct_value] rather than [misperceived_value], is the reasoning in step k valid?'; (c) if the reasoning IS locally valid (confirmed by 2/3 VLMs), label step k as a CASCADE error; (d) if the reasoning is NOT locally valid, label as a direct error (reasoning, calculation, etc.). This counterfactual test provides an objective, testable definition unprecedented in the multimodal PRM literature.

(Phase A) Gold-Standard Benchmark -- VisualProcessBench-Cascade: Extend VisualProcessBench's 2,866 samples (~8,000 incorrect steps) with cascade annotations. The cascade category is operationalized via the counterfactual question ('would this step be correct with corrected perception?'), which is more objective than purely categorical error typing.

(Phase B) Large-Scale Dataset -- VL-PRM-Cascade: Apply the automated cascade detection pipeline (Component 1) to VL-PRM300K (1.32M steps). Confidence-calibrated labeling: HIGH confidence (3/3 VLM agreement, ~70-75%) used directly; MEDIUM (2/3, ~15-20%) used with reduced weight; LOW (~10-15%) routed to human review. Validate against gold benchmark, targeting >80% cascade detection F1.

Pre-committed granularity fallback: If 3-tier kappa falls below 0.60, we report the {root-cause error vs. cascade error} binary taxonomy, which should achieve kappa > 0.70 as a binary classification with an objective counterfactual criterion. This turns a potential weakness into a controlled granularity ablation.

**Component 3: Cascade-Aware PRM Training (Weeks 7-12).**

Train multimodal PRMs (InternVL2.5-8B backbone) with five training regimes forming a granularity ladder:

(A) Binary baseline: standard correct/incorrect on VL-PRM300K.
(B) 2-way typed: {perception error, reasoning error} -- the simplest typed approach, similar in spirit to GM-PRM's dimensional separation but as explicit training labels.
(C) 3-way cascade-aware (PRIMARY MODEL): {perception, reasoning, cascade} with a two-stage prediction architecture inspired by PathFinder-PRM's hierarchical insight: first predict error type (perception/reasoning/cascade), then predict correctness conditioned on error type. For cascade errors, the model additionally predicts the root-cause step, providing interpretable error provenance.
(D) 3-way with cascade-weighted loss: same taxonomy as (C) but with cascade-specific loss weighting. Cascade errors receive higher weight because they represent the largest information gain over binary labels (a cascade step is wrong but for external reasons, requiring different correction strategies). Loss: L = sum_i w(type_i) * CE(y_i, y_hat_i) where w(cascade) > w(perception) > w(reasoning).
(E) Full fine-grained (ablation): complete sub-category decomposition for maximal information, reported for completeness.

Compare against: binary VL-PRM-7B, Perceval (binary hallucination PRM), GM-PRM (dimensional CoT), and EVPV (global reliability gating).

2	  "id": "idea_028",
3	  "source_backend": "prod_s1",
4	  "key": "corl_001_prod_s1",
5	  "title": "AffordVLA: Affordance-Level Contrastive Distillation for Efficient Dual-Grounded VLA Representations",
6	  "content": "# AffordVLA: Affordance-Level Contrastive Distillation for Efficient Dual-Grounded VLA Representations

## Core Problem
How can we produce VLA representations that are simultaneously spatially grounded at the affordance level (part-level interaction geometry, not just entity-level) and linguistically grounded (instruction-conditioned), achieving dual-grounding with zero inference overhead — where current approaches either require persistent inference-time modules (ProGAL-VLA's entity graph + symbolic planner at ~96ms/step) or address only one failure mode?

## Opportunity
LIBERO-Plus (CVPR 2026) reveals two orthogonal VLA failure modes: (1) visual brittleness — performance collapses from 95% to below 30% under perturbation, and (2) linguistic blindness — models ignore instructions entirely, relying on positional bias (confirmed by IGAR, arXiv 2603.06001). The most important recent development is ProGAL-VLA (arXiv 2604.09824, Apr 2026), which uses entity-level contrastive learning (GAC loss with InfoNCE) to address BOTH failure modes, achieving 85.5% on LIBERO-Plus — the current SOTA. However, ProGAL-VLA has three fundamental limitations: (a) it operates at entity-level granularity (grounding to 'the mug' rather than 'the mug's handle for grasping'), missing part-level interaction geometry critical for manipulation; (b) it requires a full inference pipeline (YOLO-World detector + Metric3D depth + 7B Qwen-2.5-VL planner + GSM entity graph + SACA attention, totaling ~96ms/step at 10.31 FPS); (c) its symbolic planner normalizes instructions into structured templates, losing open-vocabulary flexibility. GuidedVLA (arXiv 2605.12369, RSS 2026) adds factor-specialized attention heads but requires manually defined factor types and shows modest gains (+7.2% over π₀ baseline). Meanwhile, the probing study (arXiv 2602.20501) confirms DINOv2 encodes part-level geometric structures and VLMs contain verb-conditioned interaction priors — exactly the affordance-level signals missing from entity-level approaches. The context-dependency study (arXiv 2603.04419) shows >90% of affordance is context-dependent, arguing against fixed taxonomies. The pieces exist for an affordance-level dual-grounding approach that is simultaneously finer-grained than ProGAL-VLA's entity grounding and more efficient at inference.

## Landscape
**Dual-grounding VLAs (the direct competitor space)**: ProGAL-VLA (arXiv 2604.09824, Apr 2026) is the current LIBERO-Plus SOTA (85.5%) and the most direct competitor. It constructs a 3D entity-centric graph (GSM) using YOLO-World detection + Metric3D depth, generates symbolic sub-goals via a Qwen-2.5-VL-7B slow planner, and aligns sub-goals with entities via a Grounding Alignment Contrastive (GAC) loss (entity-level InfoNCE: positive pairs are (sub-goal, corresponding entity), negatives are other scene entities). It reduces language ignorance 3-4× and achieves 93.2% on camera, 71.5% on robot, 93.6% on language perturbations. Critical limitations: (1) entity-level granularity — contrasts whole objects, not object parts or interaction regions; for 'grasp the mug by its handle,' ProGAL grounds to the mug entity, not the handle affordance region; (2) full inference pipeline required (detector 43ms + GSM 15.8ms + SACA 10.7ms + policy 26.9ms = ~96ms/step); (3) relies on pretrained detection components whose errors propagate as grounding failures (acknowledged limitation); (4) symbolic planner normalizes linguistic variability into structured templates, limiting open-vocabulary generalization. **Factor-specialized VLAs**: GuidedVLA (arXiv 2605.12369, RSS 2026) uses ControlNet-style residual adapters on π₀ to specialize attention heads for three manually defined factors: object grounding (Qwen3-VL + SAM2 masks + human verification), spatial geometry (DA3 depth encoder), and temporal skill logic (KL-divergence against soft skill labels). Achieves 75.4% on LIBERO-Plus (+7.2% over π₀). Limitations: requires manual factor taxonomy definition, does not use contrastive learning (no appearance-invariance structure), auxiliary heads remain active at inference (ControlNet residual), and requires human verification in supervision pipeline. **Affordance-integrated VLAs with fixed taxonomies**: PALM (arXiv 2601.07060, Jan 2026) structures policy around 4 predefined affordance types (object relevance, contact geometry, spatial placement, motion dynamics) with external tool supervision (GroundingDINO, SAM, SpatialVLM, CoTracker). Affordance queries attend over language, vision, and state tokens via cross-attention — the prediction within each type IS instruction-conditioned. The genuine limitation is that the 4 affordance types are a fixed predefined taxonomy: the model cannot discover novel interaction types beyond these 4 categories, limiting generalization to unseen manipulation verbs. Achieves 94.5% avg on standard LIBERO, 91.8% on LIBERO-LONG, but no LIBERO-Plus evaluation reported. CoA-VLA (ICCV 2025, arXiv 2412.20451) uses chain-of-affordance reasoning over 4 predefined types but underperforms PALM. **Multi-auxiliary VLAs (the saturated paradigm)**: SG-VLA (arXiv 2603.22760, Mar 2026) co-trains 5 auxiliary decoders (robot position, joint configs, binary grasp classification, relative pose, segmentation) on a 1.3B VLA — grasp affordance is binary task-specific (grasped/not-grasped), not open-vocabulary spatial prediction conditioned on instruction semantics. QDepth-VLA (arXiv 2510.14836) adds depth prediction via VQ-VAE — captures 3D geometry but not interaction semantics (a flat surface and a button have the same depth but different affordances). DreamVLA (NeurIPS 2025, arXiv 2507.04447) predicts dynamic region masks, depth, and semantic features. RS-CL (arXiv 2510.01711) uses robot-state contrastive loss — aligns with proprioceptive state, not spatial affordance. ReconVLA (arXiv 2508.10333) reconstructs gaze regions via diffusion transformer. GeoVLA (arXiv 2508.09071) injects 3D point cloud representations. **Why affordance-level auxiliary loss is qualitatively different from all of the above**: The field now has 7+ concurrent auxiliary-loss VLA variants, each targeting different representational signals. The critical structural argument: affordance encodes *interaction geometry* — how an agent can interact with specific parts of an object — which occupies a unique position in representational space. Unlike depth (QDepth-VLA, GuidedVLA's geometry head), which captures 3D structure without interaction semantics (a mug handle and a mug body may have similar depth profiles but fundamentally different grasp affordances), affordance representations are *action-relevant*. Unlike entity-level grounding (ProGAL-VLA), which identifies WHAT object to interact with, affordance-level grounding identifies WHERE on the object and HOW to interact — the handle region for grasping vs. the rim for pouring. Unlike factor-guided attention (GuidedVLA), which requires manual factor taxonomy, affordance-type contrastive clustering automatically discovers interaction structure from instruction verbs. Unlike robot-state alignment (RS-CL), which grounds representations in proprioceptive space, affordance grounds them in the visual-spatial interaction space. The probing study (arXiv 2602.20501) provides direct evidence: DINOv2's part-level geometric prototypes and VLMs' verb-conditioned interaction priors are compositionally separable — affordance sits at their intersection, encoding part geometry conditioned on interaction semantics. The context-dependency finding (arXiv 2603.04419, >90% context-dependent) confirms this is not reducible to fixed object categories. **Attention-based VLAs without affordance supervision**: FocusVLA (arXiv 2603.28740, Mar 2026) proposes top-K visual token selection, achieving 98.7% on standard LIBERO but with zero affordance signal and no LIBERO-Plus evaluation. AVA-VLA (arXiv 2511.18960) uses history-conditioned active visual attention; LIBERO+CALVIN SOTA. DeepVision-VLA (arXiv 2603.15618) injects multi-level vision features. **Robustness-focused VLAs**: RobustVLA (ICLR 2026, arXiv 2510.00037) uses RL post-training with Jacobian/smoothness regularization — +12.6% across 17 perturbation types but without affordance grounding. VLA-GSE (arXiv 2605.06175) achieves 81.2% LIBERO-Plus with only 2.51% trainable parameters — the PEFT robustness SOTA. **Language grounding in VLAs**: IGAR (arXiv 2603.06001) reveals linguistic blindness as attention sink problem, proposes train-free attention recalibration (+40 LGS points). ST4VLA (ICLR 2026, arXiv 2602.10109) shows spatial grounding pre-training improves both robustness and language sensitivity. Stable Language Guidance (arXiv 2601.04052) identifies modality collapse where affordance priors overwhelm language. **Modular affordance pipelines**: UAD (arXiv 2506.09284, ICRA 2025 Best Paper Finalist) distills affordance pseudo-labels from frozen VLMs unsupervised. AFI (arXiv 2512.07472) uses 3D Spatial Affordance Fields as inference-time plug-in (+23.5% OOD), proving affordance helps robustness but requiring a persistent external module. **The refined gap**: ProGAL-VLA proves that contrastive dual-grounding improves VLA robustness. But it operates at entity-level with a heavy inference pipeline. No existing work (1) distills open-vocabulary instruction-conditioned affordance at the part/interaction-geometry level into VLA intermediate representations, (2) uses contrastive learning to cluster representations by interaction type rather than entity identity, AND (3) achieves this with zero inference overhead. AffordVLA fills this specific gap: affordance-level dual-grounding that is finer-grained than ProGAL-VLA's entity grounding, more automatic than GuidedVLA's manual taxonomy, more open-vocabulary than PALM's 4 fixed types, and more efficient than any modular approach.

## Description
Current VLAs suffer two orthogonal failures: visual brittleness (95%→30% under perturbation, LIBERO-Plus CVPR 2026) and linguistic blindness (models ignore instructions, IGAR arXiv 2603.06001). ProGAL-VLA (Apr 2026) addresses both via entity-level contrastive learning (GAC loss), achieving 85.5% LIBERO-Plus SOTA — but at the cost of a full inference pipeline (YOLO-World + Metric3D + 7B planner + entity graph, ~96ms/step) and with only entity-level granularity (grounding to 'the mug' rather than 'the mug's handle for grasping'). GuidedVLA (RSS 2026) specializes attention heads for manually defined factors but achieves only 75.4% and requires human verification in supervision. PALM uses instruction-conditioned prediction within 4 predefined affordance types but cannot discover novel interaction categories. We propose AffordVLA, which achieves dual-grounding at the affordance level — finer-grained, more efficient, and more automatic than existing approaches. Two complementary losses distill open-vocabulary affordance from frozen foundation models into VLA intermediate representations: (1) an affordance prediction loss forces instruction-conditioned spatial heatmaps at part level, combating linguistic blindness; (2) a contrastive interaction-type loss clusters features by interaction geometry (grasp vs. press vs. slide) rather than object appearance or entity identity, combating visual brittleness. The core insight is that neither loss alone achieves dual-grounding: prediction without contrastive gives instruction-conditioned but visually brittle features; contrastive without prediction gives appearance-invariant but spatially imprecise features. Their combination produces representations that are simultaneously spatially grounded at part level and appearance-invariant — qualitatively different from depth (no interaction semantics), entity grounding (no part-level specificity), or factor-guided attention (no automatic interaction discovery). Unlike ProGAL-VLA's entity-level contrastive learning, AffordVLA contrasts interaction-type features at the affordance level — encoding WHERE on an object and HOW to interact, not just WHICH object. Interaction types are automatically extracted from instruction verbs (no symbolic planner, no manual taxonomy). A quality-filtered pseudo-label pipeline (confidence thresholding + instruction-paraphrase consistency) addresses noise without human verification. Both auxiliary heads are dropped at inference (zero overhead vs. ProGAL's ~96ms/step). Built on OpenVLA-OFT with LoRA (~8M added parameters, 0.1% of 7B base), fitting within 200 H100-hours. Evaluation centers on LIBERO-Plus comparison with ProGAL-VLA (primary), GuidedVLA, and VLA-GSE; ICBench linguistic grounding; and critical ablations: (a) prediction-only vs. contrastive-only vs. both (dual-grounding hypothesis), (b) affordance-level vs. entity-level contrastive (granularity hypothesis), (c) inference latency comparison.

## Approach
We propose AffordVLA, which distills open-vocabulary affordance knowledge from frozen foundation models into a VLA's intermediate representations via two complementary losses — producing features grounded at the affordance level (part-level interaction geometry) rather than the entity level (ProGAL-VLA) or predefined factor level (GuidedVLA/PALM), with zero inference overhead. The core theoretical insight — and the key structural contribution — is that neither auxiliary loss alone achieves dual-grounding: the affordance prediction loss provides instruction-conditioned spatial grounding (combating linguistic blindness by requiring joint vision-language attention to produce instruction-specific heatmaps), while the contrastive interaction-type loss provides appearance-invariant clustering (combating visual brittleness by organizing representations by HOW to interact rather than WHAT things look like). Prediction without contrastive gives instruction-conditioned but visually brittle features (heatmaps shift under visual perturbation); contrastive without prediction gives appearance-invariant but spatially imprecise features (interaction-type clusters without spatial localization). Their combination is necessary and sufficient for dual-grounding. The approach has three stages:

**Stage 1 — Quality-Filtered Affordance Pseudo-Label Generation (offline, one-time):** For each (image, language instruction) pair in training data, we generate dense affordance heatmaps using frozen foundation models. Following the probing study (arXiv 2602.20501), we fuse DINOv2 geometric part features (extracted via attention-based part prototypes) with a frozen VLM's (Qwen2-VL-7B) instruction-conditioned interaction priors. Concretely: (a) prompt the VLM with image and instruction to generate a textual affordance description (e.g., 'grasp the mug by its handle'), (b) use frozen GroundingDINO to project this into a spatial heatmap. To address pseudo-label noise (GroundingDINO's known hallucination and mislocalization issues — also acknowledged as a failure mode for ProGAL-VLA's YOLO-World detector), we apply two quality filters: (i) Confidence thresholding — discard heatmaps where GroundingDINO detection confidence < 0.5; (ii) Consistency checking — for each sample, generate a second heatmap using a paraphrased instruction (VLM-generated paraphrase), and retain only samples where the IoU between the two heatmaps exceeds 0.3 (same affordance region should be highlighted regardless of phrasing). Remaining pseudo-labels use soft confidence weighting rather than hard binary masks. Additionally, for each instruction we generate 2-3 VLM paraphrases of the affordance description, enabling affordance-aware data augmentation during training — a strategy impossible with PALM's fixed 4 types or GuidedVLA's manual factor definitions. No manual annotations needed (unlike GuidedVLA's Qwen3-VL + SAM2 + human verification pipeline).

**Stage 2 — Dual-Loss Affordance-Distilled Training:** Built on OpenVLA-OFT (SigLIP + DINOv2 dual encoder, 7B pretrained), we add two lightweight components: (A) Affordance Prediction Head — a 3-layer MLP (~2M parameters) reading from intermediate VLM layers 16-20 (where VLA-Adapter confirms action-generation utility peaks) that predicts the affordance heatmap, supervised by confidence-weighted focal loss against pseudo-labels. This head requires the model to jointly attend to instruction semantics and visual features to produce instruction-specific spatial predictions — directly combating linguistic blindness. Unlike PALM, whose 4 affordance types are a fixed predefined taxonomy (object relevance, contact geometry, spatial placement, motion dynamics) even though the prediction within each type is instruction-conditioned, AffordVLA's affordance space is entirely open-vocabulary: the heatmap content is dynamically determined by instruction text, enabling the model to ground novel interaction verbs unseen during training. (B) Contrastive Interaction-Type Loss — the key differentiator from both PALM and ProGAL-VLA. We extract intermediate features from affordance-highlighted regions (top-20% of heatmap) and apply an InfoNCE-style contrastive loss: positive pairs are features from the same interaction verb/type (e.g., 'grasp handle' on different objects or under different visual conditions); negative pairs are different interaction types (e.g., 'grasp' vs. 'press' vs. 'slide'). This differs fundamentally from ProGAL-VLA's GAC loss in what is contrasted: ProGAL contrasts (sub-goal, entity) pairs at the whole-object level (which mug?), while AffordVLA contrasts interaction-type features at the affordance level (grasping vs. pressing, regardless of which object). This finer granularity means AffordVLA's representations encode WHERE on an object and HOW to interact (the handle region for grasping), not just WHICH object. Interaction types are automatically extracted from instruction verbs — no manual taxonomy (unlike GuidedVLA's 3 predefined factors) and no symbolic planner (unlike ProGAL-VLA's Qwen-2.5-VL-7B planner). This contrastive loss explicitly enforces that representations cluster by interaction geometry rather than object appearance, producing features inherently invariant to visual perturbations. The total loss is L = L_action + λ_pred · L_afford_pred + λ_contrast · L_afford_contrast, with λ_pred=0.1, λ_contrast=0.05. **Both auxiliary components are dropped at inference (zero overhead)** — a critical efficiency advantage over ProGAL-VLA (~96ms/step with full inference pipeline) and GuidedVLA (ControlNet residual remains active). The VLM backbone is fine-tuned with LoRA (rank 32, ~5M parameters). Total added training parameters: ~8M (~0.1% of the 7B base).

**Stage 3 — Evaluation designed to test affordance-level dual-grounding hypothesis:** Primary benchmark: LIBERO-Plus (7 perturbation dimensions). Secondary: standard LIBERO (regression check), ICBench (language grounding diagnostic from IGAR paper), and novel instruction sets with unseen interaction verbs (open-vocabulary generalization test). **Baselines**: (1) **ProGAL-VLA** (entity-level contrastive dual-grounding, LIBERO-Plus SOTA 85.5% — primary differentiation target), (2) **GuidedVLA** (factor-specialized attention, RSS 2026, 75.4% LIBERO-Plus), (3) **PALM** (structured affordance, 4 fixed types), (4) **SG-VLA** (multi-auxiliary including binary grasp), (5) **FocusVLA** (generic attention), (6) **AVA-VLA** (history-conditioned attention), (7) **OpenVLA-OFT** (base model), (8) **VLA-GSE** (PEFT robustness SOTA, 81.2% LIBERO-Plus), (9) **RobustVLA** (RL post-training robustness), (10) **AFI** (inference-time affordance), (11) **AffordVLA + AFI** (training + inference-time affordance, to test complementarity). **Key ablations**: (a) Full AffordVLA vs. prediction-loss-only (no contrastive) vs. contrastive-only (no prediction) — this is the central ablation testing the dual-grounding hypothesis: prediction-only should improve linguistic grounding (ICBench) but not visual robustness (LIBERO-Plus perturbations); contrastive-only should improve visual robustness but not linguistic grounding; only the combination should improve both; (b) Affordance-level contrastive (ours) vs. entity-level contrastive (ProGAL-style, contrasting whole-object features rather than affordance-region features) — directly testing whether finer granularity matters; (c) Instruction-conditioned affordance vs. instruction-agnostic affordance (same heatmap regardless of instruction) — testing whether language conditioning drives robustness; (d) Pseudo-label quality: raw vs. confidence-filtered vs. consistency-filtered vs. both filters — quantifying noise robustness; (e) Layer selection (8/12/16/20/24) for affordance head; (f) λ_pred and λ_contrast sensitivity; (g) Qualitative visualization: attention maps under perturbation comparing AffordVLA vs. ProGAL-VLA vs. GuidedVLA vs. FocusVLA, showing that affordance-level contrastive features maintain interaction-type clustering under visual shift while entity-level features drift; (h) ICBench linguistic grounding score before/after affordance training; (i) Inference latency comparison: AffordVLA (zero overhead) vs. ProGAL-VLA (~96ms/step) vs. AFI (external module) — critical for real-world deployment. The ProGAL-VLA comparison is the most critical: if AffordVLA matches or exceeds ProGAL's 85.5% LIBERO-Plus with zero inference overhead, the efficiency argument is decisive; if AffordVLA shows superior per-dimension results on interaction-geometry-sensitive perturbations (robot, layout) while ProGAL excels on entity-identity-sensitive perturbations (camera, lighting), the granularity argument is validated. Ablation (b) specifically tests whether affordance-level contrastive outperforms entity-level contrastive on the same backbone, isolating the granularity contribution.

  "content": "# AffordVLA: Affordance-Level Contrastive Distillation for Efficient Dual-Grounded VLA Representations

## Core Problem
How can we produce VLA representations that are simultaneously spatially grounded at the affordance level (part-level interaction geometry, not just entity-level) and linguistically grounded (instruction-conditioned), achieving dual-grounding with zero inference overhead — where current approaches either require persistent inference-time modules (ProGAL-VLA's entity graph + symbolic planner at ~96ms/step) or address only one failure mode?

## Opportunity
LIBERO-Plus (CVPR 2026) reveals two orthogonal VLA failure modes: (1) visual brittleness — performance collapses from 95% to below 30% under perturbation, and (2) linguistic blindness — models ignore instructions entirely, relying on positional bias (confirmed by IGAR, arXiv 2603.06001). The most important recent development is ProGAL-VLA (arXiv 2604.09824, Apr 2026), which uses entity-level contrastive learning (GAC loss with InfoNCE) to address BOTH failure modes, achieving 85.5% on LIBERO-Plus — the current SOTA. However, ProGAL-VLA has three fundamental limitations: (a) it operates at entity-level granularity (grounding to 'the mug' rather than 'the mug's handle for grasping'), missing part-level interaction geometry critical for manipulation; (b) it requires a full inference pipeline (YOLO-World detector + Metric3D depth + 7B Qwen-2.5-VL planner + GSM entity graph + SACA attention, totaling ~96ms/step at 10.31 FPS); (c) its symbolic planner normalizes instructions into structured templates, losing open-vocabulary flexibility. GuidedVLA (arXiv 2605.12369, RSS 2026) adds factor-specialized attention heads but requires manually defined factor types and shows modest gains (+7.2% over π₀ baseline). Meanwhile, the probing study (arXiv 2602.20501) confirms DINOv2 encodes part-level geometric structures and VLMs contain verb-conditioned interaction priors — exactly the affordance-level signals missing from entity-level approaches. The context-dependency study (arXiv 2603.04419) shows >90% of affordance is context-dependent, arguing against fixed taxonomies. The pieces exist for an affordance-level dual-grounding approach that is simultaneously finer-grained than ProGAL-VLA's entity grounding and more efficient at inference.

## Landscape
**Dual-grounding VLAs (the direct competitor space)**: ProGAL-VLA (arXiv 2604.09824, Apr 2026) is the current LIBERO-Plus SOTA (85.5%) and the most direct competitor. It constructs a 3D entity-centric graph (GSM) using YOLO-World detection + Metric3D depth, generates symbolic sub-goals via a Qwen-2.5-VL-7B slow planner, and aligns sub-goals with entities via a Grounding Alignment Contrastive (GAC) loss (entity-level InfoNCE: positive pairs are (sub-goal, corresponding entity), negatives are other scene entities). It reduces language ignorance 3-4× and achieves 93.2% on camera, 71.5% on robot, 93.6% on language perturbations. Critical limitations: (1) entity-level granularity — contrasts whole objects, not object parts or interaction regions; for 'grasp the mug by its handle,' ProGAL grounds to the mug entity, not the handle affordance region; (2) full inference pipeline required (detector 43ms + GSM 15.8ms + SACA 10.7ms + policy 26.9ms = ~96ms/step); (3) relies on pretrained detection components whose errors propagate as grounding failures (acknowledged limitation); (4) symbolic planner normalizes linguistic variability into structured templates, limiting open-vocabulary generalization. **Factor-specialized VLAs**: GuidedVLA (arXiv 2605.12369, RSS 2026) uses ControlNet-style residual adapters on π₀ to specialize attention heads for three manually defined factors: object grounding (Qwen3-VL + SAM2 masks + human verification), spatial geometry (DA3 depth encoder), and temporal skill logic (KL-divergence against soft skill labels). Achieves 75.4% on LIBERO-Plus (+7.2% over π₀). Limitations: requires manual factor taxonomy definition, does not use contrastive learning (no appearance-invariance structure), auxiliary heads remain active at inference (ControlNet residual), and requires human verification in supervision pipeline. **Affordance-integrated VLAs with fixed taxonomies**: PALM (arXiv 2601.07060, Jan 2026) structures policy around 4 predefined affordance types (object relevance, contact geometry, spatial placement, motion dynamics) with external tool supervision (GroundingDINO, SAM, SpatialVLM, CoTracker). Affordance queries attend over language, vision, and state tokens via cross-attention — the prediction within each type IS instruction-conditioned. The genuine limitation is that the 4 affordance types are a fixed predefined taxonomy: the model cannot discover novel interaction types beyond these 4 categories, limiting generalization to unseen manipulation verbs. Achieves 94.5% avg on standard LIBERO, 91.8% on LIBERO-LONG, but no LIBERO-Plus evaluation reported. CoA-VLA (ICCV 2025, arXiv 2412.20451) uses chain-of-affordance reasoning over 4 predefined types but underperforms PALM. **Multi-auxiliary VLAs (the saturated paradigm)**: SG-VLA (arXiv 2603.22760, Mar 2026) co-trains 5 auxiliary decoders (robot position, joint configs, binary grasp classification, relative pose, segmentation) on a 1.3B VLA — grasp affordance is binary task-specific (grasped/not-grasped), not open-vocabulary spatial prediction conditioned on instruction semantics. QDepth-VLA (arXiv 2510.14836) adds depth prediction via VQ-VAE — captures 3D geometry but not interaction semantics (a flat surface and a button have the same depth but different affordances). DreamVLA (NeurIPS 2025, arXiv 2507.04447) predicts dynamic region masks, depth, and semantic features. RS-CL (arXiv 2510.01711) uses robot-state contrastive loss — aligns with proprioceptive state, not spatial affordance. ReconVLA (arXiv 2508.10333) reconstructs gaze regions via diffusion transformer. GeoVLA (arXiv 2508.09071) injects 3D point cloud representations. **Why affordance-level auxiliary loss is qualitatively different from all of the above**: The field now has 7+ concurrent auxiliary-loss VLA variants, each targeting different representational signals. The critical structural argument: affordance encodes *interaction geometry* — how an agent can interact with specific parts of an object — which occupies a unique position in representational space. Unlike depth (QDepth-VLA, GuidedVLA's geometry head), which captures 3D structure without interaction semantics (a mug handle and a mug body may have similar depth profiles but fundamentally different grasp affordances), affordance representations are *action-relevant*. Unlike entity-level grounding (ProGAL-VLA), which identifies WHAT object to interact with, affordance-level grounding identifies WHERE on the object and HOW to interact — the handle region for grasping vs. the rim for pouring. Unlike factor-guided attention (GuidedVLA), which requires manual factor taxonomy, affordance-type contrastive clustering automatically discovers interaction structure from instruction verbs. Unlike robot-state alignment (RS-CL), which grounds representations in proprioceptive space, affordance grounds them in the visual-spatial interaction space. The probing study (arXiv 2602.20501) provides direct evidence: DINOv2's part-level geometric prototypes and VLMs' verb-conditioned interaction priors are compositionally separable — affordance sits at their intersection, encoding part geometry conditioned on interaction semantics. The context-dependency finding (arXiv 2603.04419, >90% context-dependent) confirms this is not reducible to fixed object categories. **Attention-based VLAs without affordance supervision**: FocusVLA (arXiv 2603.28740, Mar 2026) proposes top-K visual token selection, achieving 98.7% on standard LIBERO but with zero affordance signal and no LIBERO-Plus evaluation. AVA-VLA (arXiv 2511.18960) uses history-conditioned active visual attention; LIBERO+CALVIN SOTA. DeepVision-VLA (arXiv 2603.15618) injects multi-level vision features. **Robustness-focused VLAs**: RobustVLA (ICLR 2026, arXiv 2510.00037) uses RL post-training with Jacobian/smoothness regularization — +12.6% across 17 perturbation types but without affordance grounding. VLA-GSE (arXiv 2605.06175) achieves 81.2% LIBERO-Plus with only 2.51% trainable parameters — the PEFT robustness SOTA. **Language grounding in VLAs**: IGAR (arXiv 2603.06001) reveals linguistic blindness as attention sink problem, proposes train-free attention recalibration (+40 LGS points). ST4VLA (ICLR 2026, arXiv 2602.10109) shows spatial grounding pre-training improves both robustness and language sensitivity. Stable Language Guidance (arXiv 2601.04052) identifies modality collapse where affordance priors overwhelm language. **Modular affordance pipelines**: UAD (arXiv 2506.09284, ICRA 2025 Best Paper Finalist) distills affordance pseudo-labels from frozen VLMs unsupervised. AFI (arXiv 2512.07472) uses 3D Spatial Affordance Fields as inference-time plug-in (+23.5% OOD), proving affordance helps robustness but requiring a persistent external module. **The refined gap**: ProGAL-VLA proves that contrastive dual-grounding improves VLA robustness. But it operates at entity-level with a heavy inference pipeline. No existing work (1) distills open-vocabulary instruction-conditioned affordance at the part/interaction-geometry level into VLA intermediate representations, (2) uses contrastive learning to cluster representations by interaction type rather than entity identity, AND (3) achieves this with zero inference overhead. AffordVLA fills this specific gap: affordance-level dual-grounding that is finer-grained than ProGAL-VLA's entity grounding, more automatic than GuidedVLA's manual taxonomy, more open-vocabulary than PALM's 4 fixed types, and more efficient than any modular approach.

## Description
Current VLAs suffer two orthogonal failures: visual brittleness (95%→30% under perturbation, LIBERO-Plus CVPR 2026) and linguistic blindness (models ignore instructions, IGAR arXiv 2603.06001). ProGAL-VLA (Apr 2026) addresses both via entity-level contrastive learning (GAC loss), achieving 85.5% LIBERO-Plus SOTA — but at the cost of a full inference pipeline (YOLO-World + Metric3D + 7B planner + entity graph, ~96ms/step) and with only entity-level granularity (grounding to 'the mug' rather than 'the mug's handle for grasping'). GuidedVLA (RSS 2026) specializes attention heads for manually defined factors but achieves only 75.4% and requires human verification in supervision. PALM uses instruction-conditioned prediction within 4 predefined affordance types but cannot discover novel interaction categories. We propose AffordVLA, which achieves dual-grounding at the affordance level — finer-grained, more efficient, and more automatic than existing approaches. Two complementary losses distill open-vocabulary affordance from frozen foundation models into VLA intermediate representations: (1) an affordance prediction loss forces instruction-conditioned spatial heatmaps at part level, combating linguistic blindness; (2) a contrastive interaction-type loss clusters features by interaction geometry (grasp vs. press vs. slide) rather than object appearance or entity identity, combating visual brittleness. The core insight is that neither loss alone achieves dual-grounding: prediction without contrastive gives instruction-conditioned but visually brittle features; contrastive without prediction gives appearance-invariant but spatially imprecise features. Their combination produces representations that are simultaneously spatially grounded at part level and appearance-invariant — qualitatively different from depth (no interaction semantics), entity grounding (no part-level specificity), or factor-guided attention (no automatic interaction discovery). Unlike ProGAL-VLA's entity-level contrastive learning, AffordVLA contrasts interaction-type features at the affordance level — encoding WHERE on an object and HOW to interact, not just WHICH object. Interaction types are automatically extracted from instruction verbs (no symbolic planner, no manual taxonomy). A quality-filtered pseudo-label pipeline (confidence thresholding + instruction-paraphrase consistency) addresses noise without human verification. Both auxiliary heads are dropped at inference (zero overhead vs. ProGAL's ~96ms/step). Built on OpenVLA-OFT with LoRA (~8M added parameters, 0.1% of 7B base), fitting within 200 H100-hours. Evaluation centers on LIBERO-Plus comparison with ProGAL-VLA (primary), GuidedVLA, and VLA-GSE; ICBench linguistic grounding; and critical ablations: (a) prediction-only vs. contrastive-only vs. both (dual-grounding hypothesis), (b) affordance-level vs. entity-level contrastive (granularity hypothesis), (c) inference latency comparison.

## Approach
We propose AffordVLA, which distills open-vocabulary affordance knowledge from frozen foundation models into a VLA's intermediate representations via two complementary losses — producing features grounded at the affordance level (part-level interaction geometry) rather than the entity level (ProGAL-VLA) or predefined factor level (GuidedVLA/PALM), with zero inference overhead. The core theoretical insight — and the key structural contribution — is that neither auxiliary loss alone achieves dual-grounding: the affordance prediction loss provides instruction-conditioned spatial grounding (combating linguistic blindness by requiring joint vision-language attention to produce instruction-specific heatmaps), while the contrastive interaction-type loss provides appearance-invariant clustering (combating visual brittleness by organizing representations by HOW to interact rather than WHAT things look like). Prediction without contrastive gives instruction-conditioned but visually brittle features (heatmaps shift under visual perturbation); contrastive without prediction gives appearance-invariant but spatially imprecise features (interaction-type clusters without spatial localization). Their combination is necessary and sufficient for dual-grounding. The approach has three stages:

**Stage 1 — Quality-Filtered Affordance Pseudo-Label Generation (offline, one-time):** For each (image, language instruction) pair in training data, we generate dense affordance heatmaps using frozen foundation models. Following the probing study (arXiv 2602.20501), we fuse DINOv2 geometric part features (extracted via attention-based part prototypes) with a frozen VLM's (Qwen2-VL-7B) instruction-conditioned interaction priors. Concretely: (a) prompt the VLM with image and instruction to generate a textual affordance description (e.g., 'grasp the mug by its handle'), (b) use frozen GroundingDINO to project this into a spatial heatmap. To address pseudo-label noise (GroundingDINO's known hallucination and mislocalization issues — also acknowledged as a failure mode for ProGAL-VLA's YOLO-World detector), we apply two quality filters: (i) Confidence thresholding — discard heatmaps where GroundingDINO detection confidence < 0.5; (ii) Consistency checking — for each sample, generate a second heatmap using a paraphrased instruction (VLM-generated paraphrase), and retain only samples where the IoU between the two heatmaps exceeds 0.3 (same affordance region should be highlighted regardless of phrasing). Remaining pseudo-labels use soft confidence weighting rather than hard binary masks. Additionally, for each instruction we generate 2-3 VLM paraphrases of the affordance description, enabling affordance-aware data augmentation during training — a strategy impossible with PALM's fixed 4 types or GuidedVLA's manual factor definitions. No manual annotations needed (unlike GuidedVLA's Qwen3-VL + SAM2 + human verification pipeline).

**Stage 2 — Dual-Loss Affordance-Distilled Training:** Built on OpenVLA-OFT (SigLIP + DINOv2 dual encoder, 7B pretrained), we add two lightweight components: (A) Affordance Prediction Head — a 3-layer MLP (~2M parameters) reading from intermediate VLM layers 16-20 (where VLA-Adapter confirms action-generation utility peaks) that predicts the affordance heatmap, supervised by confidence-weighted focal loss against pseudo-labels. This head requires the model to jointly attend to instruction semantics and visual features to produce instruction-specific spatial predictions — directly combating linguistic blindness. Unlike PALM, whose 4 affordance types are a fixed predefined taxonomy (object relevance, contact geometry, spatial placement, motion dynamics) even though the prediction within each type is instruction-conditioned, AffordVLA's affordance space is entirely open-vocabulary: the heatmap content is dynamically determined by instruction text, enabling the model to ground novel interaction verbs unseen during training. (B) Contrastive Interaction-Type Loss — the key differentiator from both PALM and ProGAL-VLA. We extract intermediate features from affordance-highlighted regions (top-20% of heatmap) and apply an InfoNCE-style contrastive loss: positive pairs are features from the same interaction verb/type (e.g., 'grasp handle' on different objects or under different visual conditions); negative pairs are different interaction types (e.g., 'grasp' vs. 'press' vs. 'slide'). This differs fundamentally from ProGAL-VLA's GAC loss in what is contrasted: ProGAL contrasts (sub-goal, entity) pairs at the whole-object level (which mug?), while AffordVLA contrasts interaction-type features at the affordance level (grasping vs. pressing, regardless of which object). This finer granularity means AffordVLA's representations encode WHERE on an object and HOW to interact (the handle region for grasping), not just WHICH object. Interaction types are automatically extracted from instruction verbs — no manual taxonomy (unlike GuidedVLA's 3 predefined factors) and no symbolic planner (unlike ProGAL-VLA's Qwen-2.5-VL-7B planner).
